s1.syndrome_frame: Sepsis with multiple sites of infection and organ involvement
key_facts: 52-year-old male patient
Alcohol use disorder
Newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes with hemoglobin A1c of 7.5%
No history or findings suggestive of cirrhosis
No travel outside Southern California
Blood and wound cultures grew Klebsiella pneumoniae
Positive string test
Organism resistant only to ampicillin
MRI showed osteomyelitis and abscesses in multiple bones
Abdominal Ultrasound revealed a large liver abscess
Bone Scan showed increased uptake in multiple bones
Right femur biopsy demonstrated abscess formation

raw.rationale: The patient's blood and wound cultures grew Klebsiella pneumoniae, and the organism showed resistance only to ampicillin, which is a key fact that points to this infection as the primary cause of the patient's condition.

rejected.label: Diabetic foot infection
rejected.why: While the patient has newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes, the presence of Klebsiella pneumoniae in blood and wound cultures and the positive string test suggest a more specific infectious cause.

rejected.label: Osteomyelitis
rejected.why: Osteomyelitis is a complication of the infection, as shown by MRI and bone scan results, but it is not the primary cause.

rejected.label: Liver abscess
rejected.why: The liver abscess is likely a complication of the Klebsiella pneumoniae infection, as suggested by the abdominal ultrasound findings.

rejected.label: Septic shock
rejected.why: Septic shock is a consequence of the infection, rather than the primary cause, which is the Klebsiella pneumoniae infection itself.

gold: Hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae (hvKp) infection with multifocal manifestations including bacteremia, tibial osteomyelitis, pyogenic liver abscess, and multifocal osteomyelitis
